markdown_report:
At 0% progress, select **recent-prefix top-10 auxiliary supervision**: preserve the corrected NextItNet and add one training loss on recent prefixes. This is a testable proposal; no new training or validation results are available.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Recent, specific connections attract users; broadly related recommendations often displace them. Recent-prefix supervision targets this distinction indirectly through observed next items. (2) Older isolated interests persist in recommendations. Cropping removes older evidence during auxiliary training, although useful long-term preferences can also be lost. (3) Electronics has 12.27% sampled negative wins and a −0.2595 lower-tail margin. This motivates ranking supervision, without establishing validation performance. (4) Mapped embedding similarities near 0.5 correspond to near-zero mean cosine similarity. They provide little evidence for a collapse intervention.

**Literature insights.** SoftmaxLoss@K motivates cutoff-focused optimization, but its NDCG guarantees do not transfer to HR@10. Differentiable Fast Top-K motivates membership surrogates, with unproven transfer from cascade recommendation. Subbiah et al. establish that sampling affects rank objectives; catalog-rank correction is inappropriate to assume for this sampled-candidate benchmark. Recformer motivates text sharing, but does not establish effectiveness without pretrained weights.

| Direction | Existing approach | Practical gap |
|---|---|---|
| Context selection | Supplied suffix supervision; NextItNet | Recent evidence can be ambiguous |
| Ranking objective | CE; SoftmaxLoss@K; soft top-k | Pairwise separation does not target tenth place |
| Item specificity | Recformer-inspired text sharing | No compatibility or purpose labels |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Recent-prefix cutoff auxiliary: 4/7/7/8/5.** Positive: links recent evidence to the top-10 boundary. Negative: cropping and order-statistic losses are established ingredients; user benefits remain hypotheses.
- **Full-prefix cutoff auxiliary: 3/6/4/8/3.** Positive: isolates ranking-objective effects cheaply. Negative: provides no direct mechanism against persistent stale interests.
- **Joint title-token mean encoder: 3/7/6/6/6.** Positive: shares specific lexical evidence across items. Negative: lexical overlap can reinforce broad relevance and cannot establish practical fit.

**Selected algorithm.** Keep the baseline full-prefix loss. For at most one sampled valid target position per batch row, construct its recent input prefix and 99 unique uniform negatives. Add 0.25 times softplus of the tenth-highest negative score minus the positive score, with temperature 1. With distinct scores, exceeding that negative places the positive within the top ten of these training candidates. This surrogate is neither an unbiased HR estimator nor a literature guarantee.

The intervention explicitly targets stale-interest persistence and broad matches outranking specific recent matches; its model target is weak lower-tail separation. Compare against the unchanged baseline and a suffix-CE control if budget permits. Select exclusively using pinned macro validation HR@10. Deploy one complete-prefix NextItNet checkpoint per category; duplication, compatibility, and satisfied needs remain unresolved.

idea.description: Add a recent-prefix top-10-boundary auxiliary loss to the corrected NextItNet's unchanged full-prefix training objective. Train one network per category and deploy only its complete-prefix forward pass.
idea.motivation: The supplied user diagnosis reports both persistent older interests and broadly related items outranking specific recent matches. Auxiliary recent-prefix training removes older evidence for selected training examples, while a tenth-negative boundary loss concentrates additional supervision on sampled top-10 membership. These are plausible mechanisms rather than established explanations of the failures. Electronics' supplied 12.27% negative-win rate and −0.2595 tenth-percentile margin motivate improved separation; diagnostic training margins do not establish validation HR@10. At 0% progress, this small training-only extension is preferable to adding a timestamp-dependent inference interface or a text pipeline.
idea.implementation_notes:
The corrected baseline source and its constructor, sampler, training entry point, and predictor writer are absent from the supplied text. Consequently, the code below is an executable PyTorch auxiliary-loss component with an explicit integration contract, not a replacement train.py. Reconstructing the missing baseline would risk changing the supplied cold start and host interfaces. No tools, filesystem inspection, training, or validation were performed.

Preserve the baseline NextItNet backbone, full-prefix objective, optimizer, batch size, sequence length, checkpoint selection rule, and family-specific sample_batch. The sole experimental addition is loss = baseline_loss + 0.25 * auxiliary_loss. Start from the corrected cold start, not a previous trial checkpoint. Compare baseline, recent-prefix CE auxiliary, and recent-prefix boundary auxiliary sequentially only if their allocated compute fits the remaining shared budget. Each alternative is a separate experiment; never combine their predictions. The CE control uses identical crops, targets, candidates, coefficient, and temperature. It helps distinguish cutoff supervision from cropping, but does not isolate all optimization effects.

Compute the actual maximum receptive-field span from every stride-one temporal convolution on the deepest causal path: R = 1 + sum((kernel_size - 1) * dilation). Choose suffix length 8 when R > 8, otherwise max(1, R - 1); reject this context intervention if R <= 1. Verify that no sequence-wide normalization or pooling invalidates the local dependency calculation. Measure the fraction of selected positions for which cropping removes accessible evidence. A crop retaining the entire receptive field can be deterministically equivalent to the full prefix; dropout differences alone do not demonstrate historical exclusion.

For each batch row, select one uniformly random valid prediction position having more than suffix_length visible nonpadding inputs. This bounds auxiliary encoding to at most B sequences. The supplied positive at position t must be strictly after the input prefix ending at t. Copy only input positions at or before t, retain their last suffix_length nonpadding IDs, and left-pad to the baseline length. Never insert the prediction target into its own input.

For each selected position, the host integration must provide an auxiliary candidate row [positive, 99 negatives]. Draw negatives uniformly without replacement from mapped nonpadding training-catalog IDs, excluding the target and causally observed prefix positives. Do not use later training interactions, validation labels, or test labels for exclusions. Preserve the actual sampler's user/prefix mapping, including truncated-away earlier history only where already causally available. This auxiliary policy must be documented if the baseline main loss uses another support. Require at least 99 eligible negatives; skip and count unsupported rows instead of repeating IDs or silently changing the rank cutoff. Sampling without replacement must be genuine, not a fixed number of rejection attempts followed by duplicate filling. Unobserved candidates remain uncertain negatives.

The loss uses the tenth-highest score among 99 negatives, with gradients through that selected score and the positive score. Selection is differentiable almost everywhere and can produce noisy updates concentrated on one boundary negative. Temperature is fixed at 1 for the initial proposal; baseline score scale affects gradient strength. Do not detach the boundary score. No proposal-probability correction is applied: this is a deliberately sampled ranking surrogate, not an unbiased catalog objective. Its candidate count matches the evaluation count, but its causal training support and sampled users need not match the evaluator's exclusion rules or distribution. No equivalence claim is justified. Ties require the host's fixed ranking convention; the strict distinct-score membership argument alone does not settle ties.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and 200 batches per completed epoch. Use a dedicated auxiliary sampling RNG seeded 42, separate from the baseline sampler and diagnostic RNG. Preserve all four datasets and routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU and account for training, auxiliary computation, diagnostics, failures, and export checks within the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance. Four concurrent slots do not multiply that allowance. Record actual updates, processed positions, eligible/skipped crop counts, GPU seconds, parameters, peak memory, and validation queries. Additional auxiliary computation prevents simultaneous assumptions of equal updates and equal compute.

Select only through the unchanged host macro validation HR@10 protocol, with 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42. Keep the baseline validation/checkpoint schedule. Do not invent local benchmark substitutes or access hidden tests. One additional validation hit changes macro HR by 0.00125; repeated adaptive comparisons can overfit this finite sample. Freeze the configuration before final held-out evaluation. Supplied inspiration scores are contextual observations, not paired evidence for this proposal; the −1 result is not evidence identifying a particular failure cause.

Preserve ModelView.model as the actual trained nn.Module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), its metrics and metric_definitions outputs, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The diagnostic loader continues yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Auxiliary candidates remain internal to training. Measure diagnostic margins using the supplied negatives and actual deployed full-prefix features. If adding training candidate-boundary statistics, label them separately with support, temperature, candidate support, and definitions; they are not validation HR. Item-category breakdowns are unavailable because item categories are not provided. Do not fabricate them from dataset routing.

Continue the native twenty-user full-catalog unseen-item diagnosis, five real training users/category. Track stale-interest rejection, broad-match rejection, preference for a lower-ranked specific item, and uncertain item identity separately when the native output supports them. Do not infer quantitative rejection rates from qualitative summaries. This proposal needs no metadata. Only permitted histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions may be used; ratings, reviews, prices, stores, item categories, pretrained weights, and simulator traits remain unavailable.

Inference architecture is unchanged. Preserve padding-safe causal convolutions, zero padding states, and positionwise normalization. Read the final nonpadding position by positional maximum, never count minus one, and retain the corrected baseline's explicit empty-history policy. Keep the embedded predictor writer consistent with the baseline architecture/configuration/checkpoint keys. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint; there is no auxiliary inference pass, checkpoint averaging, score fusion, or separately fitted component. Verify generated-predictor reload score agreement on identical permitted inputs and all four routes. Check causal target alignment, finite auxiliary gradients, candidate uniqueness, and padding correctness with small bounded checks charged to the search budget.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def recent_prefix_auxiliary(model, sequence, positive, candidate_ids,
                            selected_positions, suffix_length,
                            temperature=1.0, control='boundary'):
    """Executable auxiliary component; host retains its baseline train.py.

    sequence, positive: B x L baseline-aligned tensors.
    selected_positions: B vector; -1 means skip this row.
    candidate_ids: B x 100; host samples [target, 99 distinct negatives]
      for each selected row from the declared causal training support.
    model.log2feats: B x L -> B x L x D.
    model.predict_score: N x D, N x 100 -> N x 100.
    Select positions and sample candidates with dedicated RNG(seed=42).
    """
    if temperature <= 0 or suffix_length < 1:
        raise ValueError('Invalid temperature or suffix length')
    if control not in ('boundary', 'ce'):
        raise ValueError('Unknown auxiliary control')
    batch_size, length = sequence.shape
    if candidate_ids.shape != (batch_size, 100):
        raise ValueError('Expected positive plus 99 negative candidate IDs')
    rows, crops = [], []
    for row in range(batch_size):
        t = int(selected_positions[row].item())
        if t < 0:
            continue
        if t >= length or sequence[row, t] == 0 or positive[row, t] == 0:
            raise ValueError('Selected position must be a valid input/target pair')
        prefix = sequence[row, :t + 1]
        visible = prefix[prefix.ne(0)]
        if visible.numel() <= suffix_length:
            continue
        ids = candidate_ids[row]
        if ids[0] != positive[row, t]:
            raise ValueError('Candidate zero must equal the aligned next target')
        if torch.any(ids <= 0) or torch.unique(ids).numel() != 100:
            raise ValueError('Candidates must be nonpadding and unique')
        if torch.isin(ids[1:], visible).any():
            raise ValueError('Negative overlaps the visible causal prefix')
        # Host also enforces any available truncated-away causal exclusions.
        crop = torch.zeros_like(sequence[row])
        recent = visible[-suffix_length:]
        crop[-recent.numel():] = recent
        rows.append(row)
        crops.append(crop)
    if not rows:
        # Adds no auxiliary gradient, preserving baseline-loss optimization.
        return model.item_emb.weight.sum() * 0.0, 0
    row_ids = torch.tensor(rows, device=sequence.device, dtype=torch.long)
    cropped_sequence = torch.stack(crops)
    features = model.log2feats(cropped_sequence)
    positions = torch.arange(length, device=sequence.device)[None, :]
    last = torch.where(cropped_sequence.ne(0), positions, -1).amax(dim=1)
    if torch.any(last < 0):
        raise ValueError('Auxiliary crops must be nonempty')
    h = features[torch.arange(len(rows), device=sequence.device), last]
    scores = model.predict_score(h, candidate_ids[row_ids])
    if scores.shape != (len(rows), 100):
        raise ValueError('Scoring adapter must return one score per candidate')
    scores = scores.float()
    if control == 'ce':
        labels = torch.zeros(len(rows), device=scores.device, dtype=torch.long)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(scores / temperature, labels)
    else:
        tenth_negative = scores[:, 1:].topk(10, dim=1).values[:, -1]
        # Keep the boundary attached to autograd.
        loss = F.softplus((tenth_negative - scores[:, 0]) / temperature).mean()
    return loss, len(rows)

# HOST INTEGRATION, preserving the supplied corrected NextItNet:
# 1. Obtain baseline sequence/positive batch and compute unchanged baseline_loss.
# 2. Per row, uniformly select an eligible causal target position, or use -1.
# 3. Sample 99 unique auxiliary negatives from the declared eligible support.
#    Skip/count rows with fewer than 99 eligible negatives; never read holdouts.
# 4. auxiliary_loss, support = recent_prefix_auxiliary(...)
# 5. loss = baseline_loss + 0.25 * auxiliary_loss
# 6. Use the unchanged optimizer, validation schedule, and checkpoint rule.
# 7. Export the unchanged architecture with one checkpoint per category.
# All epochs <= 200; 200 batches/completed epoch; training seed=42.
# Deployment uses full-prefix features and positional-maximum nonpadding readout.
# Baseline-specific sampling/training/export APIs are intentionally not invented.

originality.positive: Combines recent-prefix auxiliary training with a direct sampled tenth-negative boundary in a constrained, single-network NextItNet experiment.
originality.negative: Both supervised cropping and order-statistic ranking objectives have close precedents; this is an incremental combination, not a new intent-identification method.

future_potential.positive: A controlled comparison can determine whether recent-context supervision benefits from aligning its loss with the evaluation cutoff without increasing inference cost.
future_potential.negative: Boundary gradients can be noisy, crops can remove necessary information, and sampled top-10 gains may not improve full-catalog usefulness or resolve compatibility and duplication.

code_difficulty.positive: The added loss is small and preserves the architecture, scoring interface, and single-checkpoint predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal candidate exclusions, crop-target alignment, dedicated sampling randomness, support accounting, and host integration require care; absent baseline source prevents a complete executable train.py.

related_work.title: Next Item Recommendation with Self-Attentive? No: NextItNet, a Generative Convolutional Decoder
contributions: Provides the residual dilated causal convolution backbone retained in this proposal.
limitations: The backbone alone does not establish current purpose, compatibility, satisfied needs, or optimal sampled HR@10 supervision.

related_work.title: SoftmaxLoss@K
contributions: The supplied search material describes quantile truncation and a smooth NDCG@K surrogate, motivating cutoff-focused objectives.
limitations: Its described guarantees concern NDCG@K, not this proposal's HR@10 boundary surrogate.

related_work.title: Differentiable Fast Top-K
contributions: The supplied search material describes an O(n) approximation to top-k membership.
limitations: Reported cascade-recommendation evidence does not establish transfer to NextItNet next-item prediction; the proposed loss does not implement this operator.

related_work.title: Subbiah et al. (2024), sampled-rank bias correction
contributions: The supplied search material reports improvements from correcting sampled-rank bias in batch WARP and LambdaRank.
limitations: Catalog-rank correction cannot automatically be transferred to a benchmark explicitly ranking one positive against 99 sampled negatives.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Motivates sharing item textual information through recommendation-aware representations.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness of the alternative randomly initialized lightweight title encoder under this task's no-pretrained-weights constraint.
